name: Vessel (Anke Diallo-Sørensen)
creator: Anke Diallo-Sørensen
description: Publishing exclusively through unlicensed neural feed channels under the mononym Vessel, Diallo-Sørensen delivers spoken-word compositions that exploit BCI sensory bleed — her voice arrives accompanied by involuntary tactile and olfactory impressions she programs into the feed metadata. A piece about drowning debt makes listeners taste copper; her elegy for a the Gray Zone neighborhood demolished for a transit corridor causes phantom cold in the hands. She claims the body should be part of reading.
medium: unlicensed neural feed with embedded sensory metadata
cultural_impact: Vessel's technique has spawned an entire school of 'somatic literature' attempting to legally replicate her methods on licensed channels, invariably producing diluted corporate versions. The originals remain underground and are described by listeners as 'the difference between reading about fire and burning.'
controversy: Several listeners have reported unwanted sensory episodes hours after consuming her work, leading to debates about consent in BCI-embedded art. One corponation subsidiary has filed a patent claim on her specific metadata encoding method, attempting to legally force her underground work into licensing compliance.
story_hooks: Someone is selling Vessel recordings with corrupted metadata that produces dangerous rather than merely uncomfortable sensory effects — she needs to find them before someone is seriously hurt.
A Tier 4 corponation arts division offers her full legal protection and a licensed channel if she signs over the encoding patents — and she's considering it.
A listener claims a Vessel piece unlocked a suppressed memory that implicates a corponation in a crime — and they need someone to help them figure out if the memory is real.
